key_insight: Treating uncertainty as a learned perturbation energy and adding a lightweight post-hoc head to a frozen segmentation backbone yields accurate, calibrated failure ranking from a single forward pass.
problem_solved: Provides reliable uncertainty estimates for medical image segmentation without expensive repeated inference (ensembles/MC-dropout) or restrictive feature-space assumptions, enabling fast risk-aware contours for clinical use.
method: Post-hoc augmentation: attach a small uncertainty head to a frozen pretrained segmentation backbone so the original model stays unchanged.
Uncertainty-as-energy: the head predicts a perturbation-energy map (sensitivity/energy to hypothetical perturbations) that correlates with segmentation failure risk and calibration.
Single-pass inference and lightweight training: train the head with energy/ranking objectives on segmentation outputs so the pipeline produces risk maps and scores in one forward pass.
impact: Delivers fast, actionable uncertainty maps suitable for clinical triage and QA, reducing compute and latency compared with multi-pass methods while improving failure detection and calibration.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen segmentation backbone + lightweight uncertainty head (single forward pass) with data flow arrows
Side-by-side overlays: segmentation masks, ground-truth error map, and predicted perturbation-energy uncertainty heatmap
Performance chart: failure-detection ranking (AUROC/AUPR) comparing SegWithU vs ensembles and single-pass baselines
Efficiency bar graph: inference time / FLOPs showing single-pass cost advantage over repeated-inference methods
paper_title: SegWithU: Uncertainty as Perturbation Energy for Single-Forward-Pass Risk-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Yucheng Chen
